home.faq1Q: ¿Se suben mis archivos a un servidor?
home.faq1A: No. Todo el procesamiento se hace en tu navegador. Tus archivos no salen de tu dispositivo y no se envían a nuestros servidores ni a terceros. Aplica a todas las herramientas FileFlip: imágenes, PDF, vídeos y archivos se procesan en local.
home.faq2Q: ¿Cuál es el tamaño máximo de archivo?
home.faq2A: Los límites dependen de la memoria de tu dispositivo y del navegador. En la práctica suelen procesarse archivos de cientos de megabytes; archivos muy grandes (p. ej. más de 1 GB) pueden ralentizar el navegador o quedarse sin memoria. Si te encuentras con límites, prueba con archivos más pequeños o por lotes.
home.faq3A: Sí. FileFlip funciona en el navegador del móvil (Safari en iPhone, Chrome u otros en Android). Abres el sitio, eliges una herramienta y subes desde la galería o archivos. No hace falta instalar ninguna app. La experiencia es la misma que en el ordenador, adaptada a la pantalla.
home.faq4A: No. FileFlip necesita conexión a internet para cargar el sitio y los scripts. Una vez cargada la página, el procesamiento de archivos se hace en el navegador y no requiere conexión continua durante la conversión. Tienes que estar en línea para abrir y usar las herramientas.
home.faq5A: Entra en la herramienta «HEIC a JPG» desde la página principal. Sube uno o más archivos HEIC (p. ej. del iPhone). La herramienta los convierte en el navegador y puedes descargar cada JPG o todos en un ZIP. No hace falta cuenta ni subir a ningún servidor. La calidad se mantiene para un uso normal.
home.faq6A: Sí. Al procesarse todo en tu navegador, tus archivos no se envían a nuestros servidores ni los guardamos nosotros. Para más privacidad, usa FileFlip en un dispositivo bajo tu control y cierra la pestaña al terminar. No recogemos, guardamos ni analizamos el contenido de tus archivos.
home.faq7A: No. Puedes usar todas las herramientas de FileFlip sin registrarte ni iniciar sesión. Abre el sitio, elige una herramienta, sube el archivo y descarga el resultado. No pedimos email, contraseña ni datos personales. El uso sigue siendo sencillo y privado.
home.faq8A: Sí. FileFlip es gratis, sin costes ocultos ni planes de pago. El objetivo es ofrecer herramientas simples y prácticas para todos. No añadimos marcas de agua a los resultados ni pedimos pago. Puedes usar las herramientas tantas veces como quieras sin coste.

compressImage.label: Comprimir imagen
compressImage.short: Reduce el tamaño de tus fotos.
compressImage.metaDescription: Comprime fotos JPG, PNG y WebP online gratis. Reduce el tamaño manteniendo la calidad. Sin cuenta, todo en el navegador.
compressImage.dropzonePrompt: Arrastra aquí tu imagen o haz clic para seleccionar
compressImage.editorialTitle: Por qué comprimir imágenes, cuándo usar JPG, PNG o WebP y cómo elegir la calidad
compressImage.editorialBody:
La compresión de imágenes reduce el tamaño del archivo eliminando o simplificando parte de los datos, así tus fotos ocupan menos y cargan más rápido. Archivos más pequeños significan páginas más rápidas, adjuntos de email más ligeros y menos problemas con los límites de tamaño en formularios o redes sociales.

Elige el formato según el uso: JPG es mejor para fotos e imágenes complejas — mantiene el archivo pequeño con una pérdida visual mínima. PNG conserva cada píxel y soporta transparencia, así que úsalo para logos, capturas o gráficos con bordes definidos. WebP suele dar archivos aún más pequeños con calidad similar y lo soportan todos los navegadores modernos; úsalo cuando quieras el mejor equilibrio entre tamaño y calidad en la web.

El control de calidad regula cuánta compresión se aplica: valores más altos (p. ej. 80–90) mantienen más detalle y archivos más grandes; valores más bajos (p. ej. 50–60) reducen más el archivo pero pueden mostrar artefactos. Para la mayoría de fotos, 70–80 es un buen punto de partida — revisa la vista previa y ajusta hasta que el resultado te convenza y el tamaño se adapte a lo que necesitas.
compressImage.qualityHint: Lower = smaller file, lower quality. Try 60–80 for a good balance.
compressImage.step3Description: Save the compressed image to your device.

compressImage.faq1Q: How do you compress an image online?
compressImage.faq1A: Upload your photo (JPG, PNG or WebP) using the button, choose a quality level with the slider, then click compress. You can compare the original and compressed result side by side before downloading. Everything runs in your browser, so no data is sent to any server.
compressImage.faq2A: Compression always involves a trade-off between file size and quality. You control this with the quality slider: lower values give smaller files but more visible loss. We recommend trying 60–80 for a good balance. The preview lets you check the result before downloading.
compressImage.faq3A: You can upload and compress JPG (JPEG), PNG and WebP images. The compressed output keeps the same format as the original. These formats cover the vast majority of photos and graphics used on the web and in apps.
compressImage.faq4Q: Are files saved on the server?
compressImage.faq4A: No. All processing happens in your browser. Your images are never uploaded to our servers or stored anywhere. You stay in full control of your files from start to finish.
compressImage.faq5Q: Is there a file size limit?
compressImage.faq5A: There is no fixed limit set by the tool. Practical limits depend on your device and browser memory. Very large images (e.g. tens of megabytes) may take longer to process or, on low-memory devices, cause the browser to slow down. For typical photos (a few MB), there are no issues.
compressImage.faq6Q: What is the difference between JPG and PNG in compression?
compressImage.faq6A: JPG uses lossy compression: it discards some detail to achieve much smaller file sizes, which makes it ideal for photos. PNG uses lossless compression: it keeps every pixel intact but produces larger files, and is better for graphics with sharp edges or transparency. For photos on the web, JPG usually gives the best balance of size and quality; use PNG when you need transparency or exact reproduction of logos and UI elements.
compressImage.faq7Q: How do I compress images for WhatsApp?
compressImage.faq7A: WhatsApp automatically compresses photos when you send them, which can reduce quality. To keep control, compress your image first with this tool at a quality you choose (e.g. 75–80), then send the result: the file will be smaller and may be altered less by WhatsApp. Use JPG for photos; avoid sending huge originals so the app does not apply its own heavy compression. The tool runs in the browser, so you can do it quickly from your phone or computer before sharing.
compressImage.faq8Q: Can I compress multiple images at once?
compressImage.faq8A: Yes. You can add several images in one go: use the upload button and select multiple files, or drag and drop a batch. Each image is compressed separately and you can adjust quality per image if needed. When you are done, download each file individually or use the option to download all as a ZIP. Processing runs in your browser, so there is no limit imposed by the tool—only your device memory for very large batches.
compressImage.faq9A: No. Lossy compression (as used for JPG and WebP at lower quality) permanently removes some image data; you cannot restore the exact original from the compressed file. If you might need the full quality later, keep a copy of the original before compressing. PNG compression is lossless, so the image can be decoded back to the same pixels, but the file size reduction is smaller. This tool does not store your files, so always keep your originals on your device if you want to revert.
compressImage.faq10Q: What is the best format for photos on the web?
compressImage.faq10A: For most photos on websites and blogs, JPG is still the best choice: it gives small file sizes and good visual quality at 75–85% quality. WebP often produces even smaller files at similar quality and is supported by all modern browsers; use it when you want faster page loads. PNG is better for images with transparency or sharp graphics. Save photos as JPG or WebP for hero images, galleries, and thumbnails; use PNG for logos and graphics with transparent backgrounds.

mergePdf.label: Unir PDF
mergePdf.short: Combina varios PDF en un solo archivo.
mergePdf.metaDescription: Combina varios PDF en uno online. Arrastra para reordenar. Sin cuenta, en el navegador.
mergePdf.editorialTitle: Cuándo y por qué unir PDFs
mergePdf.editorialBody: Unir PDFs es útil cuando tienes varios documentos — informes, escaneos o formularios — que quieres en un solo archivo para compartir o imprimir. La herramienta mantiene la calidad original de cada PDF y te permite decidir el orden arrastrando los archivos. Todo se hace en el navegador, así que tus documentos no salen de tu dispositivo.
mergePdf.step1Hint: Select multiple files or add them in batches.
mergePdf.step2Hint: Drag rows to change order. Then merge.
mergePdf.pdfsPlaceholder: Your PDFs will appear here after upload.
mergePdf.step3Description: The merged PDF has been downloaded. You can merge again to download another file.
mergePdf.errorMinTwo: Upload at least two PDFs to merge.
mergePdf.errorMinTwoAlt: At least two PDFs are required to merge.
mergePdf.errorGeneric: Something went wrong. Please try again.
mergePdf.faq1Q: How do I merge PDFs online?
mergePdf.faq1A: Click the button to add one or more PDF files from your device. They appear in a list below. Drag the rows to change the order of the documents. When you are happy with the order, click "Merge PDF" to create a single PDF and download it. The process runs entirely in your browser, so your files never leave your device.
mergePdf.faq2A: You reorder whole documents, not individual pages. Drag the file rows up or down to set the order in which each PDF appears in the merged file. The pages of each PDF keep their internal order; the merged PDF is document 1's pages, then document 2's, and so on. If you need to reorder single pages within a PDF, you would need a separate tool that supports page-level editing.
mergePdf.faq3Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
mergePdf.faq3A: No. Merging is done locally in your browser. Your files never leave your device or get stored on our servers. This keeps your documents private and secure. You can merge sensitive or confidential PDFs without any upload.
mergePdf.faq4Q: Is there a limit to how many PDFs I can merge?
mergePdf.faq4A: There is no fixed limit in the tool. Very large numbers of files or very big PDFs may make the browser use a lot of memory and take longer. For typical documents (e.g. a few dozen PDFs of a few MB each), merging works without issues. If you hit performance limits, try merging in smaller batches and then merging the resulting PDFs.
mergePdf.faq5A: No. The tool combines the existing content of your PDFs without re-encoding or re-compressing the pages. Text and images in the merged PDF stay at the same quality as in the originals. The output is a single PDF that behaves like one continuous document.
mergePdf.faq6Q: Can I remove a file from the list before merging?
mergePdf.faq6A: Yes. Each file in the list has a remove or delete option so you can take it out before clicking Merge. Reorder the remaining files as needed, then merge. If you change your mind, add the file again and adjust the order.
mergePdf.faq7Q: What happens to bookmarks and links in the PDFs?
mergePdf.faq7A: Bookmarks and internal links from the original PDFs are preserved in the merged file where the library supports it. Very complex PDFs with nested bookmarks may have simplified structure in the result. External links and hyperlinks generally remain clickable in the merged PDF.
mergePdf.faq8A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser (Safari on iPhone, Chrome or others on Android). You can add PDFs from your device or cloud storage, reorder them, and download the merged file. No app install is required; processing happens in the browser so file size limits depend on your device's memory.
mergePdf.faq9A: Password-protected (encrypted) PDFs must be unlocked first before this tool can read them. Open the PDF with the correct password in another app, save it without password protection, then use that copy here. The merge tool itself does not ask for or handle PDF passwords.

heicToJpg.label: HEIC a JPG
heicToJpg.metaDescription: Convierte HEIC a JPG. Uno o más archivos, vista previa, descarga individual o ZIP.
heicToJpg.editorialTitle: Por qué convertir HEIC a JPG
heicToJpg.editorialBody: HEIC es el formato de foto por defecto en iPhone y ahorra espacio, pero muchos sitios, apps y destinatarios de email esperan JPG. Convertir a JPG hace que tus fotos sean fáciles de compartir y abrir en cualquier parte. La herramienta funciona en el navegador, así que tus fotos no salen de tu dispositivo.
heicToJpg.errorConversionFailed: Error de conversión. Prueba con otros HEIC.
heicToJpg.faq1A: HEIC is the default photo format on iPhones. Converting to JPG makes photos easier to share. Conversion runs in your browser; files never leave your device.
heicToJpg.faq2A: Yes. Select multiple HEIC files. The tool shows progress and lets you download each JPG or all in a ZIP.
heicToJpg.faq3A: JPG is lossy; there can be a small quality reduction. For typical use the result is usually very good.
heicToJpg.faq4Q: Are my photos sent to a server?
heicToJpg.faq4A: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser. Your files never leave your device.
heicToJpg.faq5A: When you convert many files, one ZIP is faster than saving each JPG individually.
heicToJpg.faq6Q: Does it work on iPhone and iPad?
heicToJpg.faq6A: Yes. Open the tool in Safari (or another browser) on your iPhone or iPad, then tap to add HEIC photos from your camera roll or Files app. The conversion runs in the browser and you can download each JPG or a ZIP. No app install is required.
heicToJpg.faq7A: Basic metadata such as date taken can be preserved when the conversion is done in the browser, depending on the library used. For full EXIF (camera model, GPS, etc.) preservation, some tools may strip or simplify it when encoding JPG. If you need exact EXIF, check the output or use a dedicated desktop tool.
heicToJpg.faq8A: The converted JPG keeps the same dimensions (pixel width and height) as the original HEIC. Only the format and compression change; resolution is not reduced. You get a standard JPG that you can use for print or web at the same size as the source.
heicToJpg.faq9Q: Can I convert HEIC to PNG or WebP instead?
heicToJpg.faq9A: This tool converts HEIC to JPG only. JPG is the most widely supported format for sharing and is sufficient for most uses. If you need PNG (e.g. for transparency) or WebP, you would need to convert HEIC to JPG first, then use another tool to convert JPG to the desired format, or use a converter that supports HEIC to PNG/WebP directly.

removeMetadata.label: Quitar metadatos
removeMetadata.short: Elimina EXIF de JPG y PNG.
removeMetadata.metaDescription: Quita todos los metadatos EXIF de imágenes. Descarga imagen limpia.
removeMetadata.faq1A: EXIF stores camera, date, GPS, etc. inside images. This tool removes all such data by redrawing the image on a clean canvas.
removeMetadata.faq2Q: Can I see metadata before removing?
removeMetadata.faq2A: Yes. The tool displays the metadata found (using exifr) so you know what will be removed. You then download the cleaned image.
removeMetadata.faq3A: No. Everything runs in your browser. Your file never leaves your device.
removeMetadata.faq4A: JPG and PNG. The image is re-encoded without EXIF; appearance is unchanged.
removeMetadata.faq5A: No. Only embedded metadata is removed. Dimensions and pixels stay the same.

pdfToPptx.label: PDF a PowerPoint
pdfToPptx.metaDescription: Convierte PDF a PowerPoint. Cada página es una slide. Descarga PPTX.
pdfToPptx.errorConversion: Error de conversión. Prueba con otro PDF.
pdfToPptx.faq1Q: How does PDF to PowerPoint work?
pdfToPptx.faq1A: Each PDF page is rendered as an image and placed on a slide. One slide per page. The tool uses pdfjs-dist and pptxgenjs in your browser.
pdfToPptx.faq2Q: Is the text editable in the PPTX?
pdfToPptx.faq2A: No. Content is embedded as images. For editable text you would need OCR or another method.
pdfToPptx.faq3Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
pdfToPptx.faq3A: No. The PDF is processed entirely in your browser.
pdfToPptx.faq4Q: What if my PDF has many pages?
pdfToPptx.faq4A: Very long PDFs take longer. The progress bar shows how many pages have been processed.
pdfToPptx.faq5Q: Can I edit the slides after?
pdfToPptx.faq5A: Yes. You get a standard PPTX. Open in PowerPoint and add text, resize, or reorder.

colorPalette.label: Paleta de colores
colorPalette.metaDescription: Extrae 6 colores dominantes. HEX, RGB, HSL. Clic para copiar.
colorPalette.colorsLabel: 6 colores dominantes (clic en HEX para copiar)
colorPalette.faq1A: The tool reads pixel data from a canvas and uses color quantization (JavaScript) to find the 6 dominant colors. It shows HEX, RGB and HSL.
colorPalette.faq2Q: Can I copy a color code?
colorPalette.faq2A: Yes. Click a color swatch to copy its HEX code to the clipboard.
colorPalette.faq3A: No. The image is processed entirely in your browser.
colorPalette.faq4A: Any format the browser can draw (JPG, PNG, WebP, etc.).
colorPalette.faq5A: Six gives a clear, usable palette. You can use them as a starting point for design.

textDiff.label: Comparar textos
textDiff.metaDescription: Compara textos. Verde añadidos, rojo eliminados. Estadísticas.
textDiff.faq1A: Paste original and modified text. The tool uses the diff library for word-by-word changes. Additions in green, removals in red. Stats: added, removed, unchanged.
textDiff.faq2A: No. Everything runs in your browser. Your text is never sent to any server.
textDiff.faq3A: There is no fixed limit. Very long texts may take a moment to process.
textDiff.faq4A: Word-level diff shows exactly which words were added or removed within a line.
textDiff.faq5A: Added: words in modified but not original. Removed: words in original but not modified. Unchanged: in both.

encryptText.label: Cifrar texto
encryptText.metaDescription: Cifra y descifra con AES-256. Contraseña nunca enviada.
encryptText.errorWrongPassword: Contraseña incorrecta o datos no válidos.
encryptText.faq1A: The tool uses crypto-js with AES-256. You enter a password; encryption runs in your browser. The password is never sent to any server.
encryptText.faq2A: No. The password is only used locally to encrypt or decrypt. You must remember it to decrypt later.
encryptText.faq3A: Yes. Copy the encrypted string and share it. The recipient needs the same password to decrypt (e.g. with this tool).
encryptText.faq4Q: What if I lose the password?
encryptText.faq4A: There is no way to recover the text without the password. Keep it in a safe place.
encryptText.faq5A: AES-256 is a strong standard. Security also depends on a strong password and not sharing it.

markdownToHtml.label: Markdown a HTML
markdownToHtml.metaDescription: Convierte Markdown a HTML. Vista previa, descarga.
markdownToHtml.faq1A: Markdown is a simple syntax for formatting text. This tool converts it to HTML with live preview and code highlighting (highlight.js).
markdownToHtml.faq2A: No. Conversion runs in your browser. Your text is never sent to any server.
markdownToHtml.faq3A: Full HTML page or just the content HTML to paste into an existing page or CMS.
markdownToHtml.faq4A: Yes. highlight.js is used for syntax highlighting in code blocks in the preview.
markdownToHtml.faq5A: The marked library supports headings, bold, italic, lists, links, images, code blocks, blockquotes, tables, etc.

qrGenerator.label: Generador QR
qrGenerator.metaDescription: Genera QR. URL, email, teléfono, WiFi. Colores, logo. PNG o SVG.
qrGenerator.faq1Q: What can I put in a QR code?
qrGenerator.faq1A: URL, text, email, phone, or WiFi. The tool has presets for URL, email, phone and WiFi.
qrGenerator.faq2A: Yes. Size, QR color, background color, and optional logo in the center. Download as PNG or SVG.
qrGenerator.faq3A: A small center logo usually still allows scanning. Very large logos can reduce reliability.
qrGenerator.faq4A: No. The QR is generated in your browser. Your content is never sent to any server.
qrGenerator.faq5A: PNG is raster; SVG is vector and scales without quality loss.

extractFrames.label: Extraer frames
extractFrames.metaDescription: Extrae frames como JPG. Descarga individual o ZIP.
extractFrames.errorLoadVideo: No se pudo cargar el video.
extractFrames.faq1A: The tool uses the HTML5 video element and canvas. It seeks to chosen times, draws each frame to canvas, and exports as JPG. No server or FFmpeg.
extractFrames.faq2A: Any format your browser can play (typically MP4). The video is read locally.
extractFrames.faq3Q: Can I choose how many frames?
extractFrames.faq3A: Yes. Set the number of frames (evenly spaced) or the interval in seconds.
extractFrames.faq4A: No. Processing is entirely in your browser.
extractFrames.faq5A: When you extract many frames, a ZIP is more convenient than saving each image one by one.

csvTools.label: Herramientas CSV
csvTools.metaDescription: Une varios CSV o divide uno por filas. Vista previa.
csvTools.mergeDesc: Sube 2 o más archivos CSV. Se usan las cabeceras del primero; las duplicadas en otros se omiten.
csvTools.splitDesc: Sube un CSV. Se dividirá en partes (cada una con este número de filas).
csvTools.faq1Q: What can the CSV tool do?
csvTools.faq1A: Merge: combine two or more CSVs into one (with optional duplicate header handling). Split: divide one CSV by row count and download parts as ZIP.
csvTools.faq2A: You can keep the first file's header and skip duplicate headers from other files. Preview before downloading.
csvTools.faq3A: PapaParse is used to read and write CSV. It handles quoted fields and different line endings.
csvTools.faq4A: No. All processing runs in your browser. Your CSVs never leave your device.
csvTools.faq5Q: Can I split by custom row count?
csvTools.faq5A: Yes. In the split tab you choose how many rows per file. The tool chunks the CSV and offers them in a ZIP.
